origin.description: Extract the first complete match from each string. When group is supplied, return that capturing group instead of the whole match.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares literal text, coll uses collation, and boundary matches character, word, line, or sentence boundaries. The empty string is a character boundary.

arguments.name: group
arguments.text: If supplied, return the text of this capturing group instead of the complete match. Group 1 is the first group. Group 0 is the whole match.

origin.details: Recycling and names follow the other stringr search functions. With group omitted, the empty pattern and boundary() extract the first boundary segment. With group set, the result is the selected column of str_match, so the pattern must be a regular expression. A miss is missing.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string or pattern, or the length of group when several groups are selected from one string.
origin.example:
shopping_list <- c("apples x4", "bag of flour", "bag of sugar", "milk x2")
str_extract(shopping_list, "([a-z]+) of ([a-z]+)", group = 1)

translation.description: Extract the first complete match from each string. When group is supplied, return that capturing group instead of the whole match.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, regex, and boundary return Pattern objects and select that engine. The empty string is a character boundary. A group argument requires a regular expression.

arguments.name: group
arguments.text: If supplied, return that capture. Group 1 is the first group, which is column index 1 of str_match. Group 0 is the whole match. A list of groups selects those columns.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. Without group, empty and bound call stri_extract_first_boundaries, and the other engines call the matching stri_extract_first function. With group, the call is str_match and then column group, because R selects column group + 1 of a 1-based matrix. A miss or a group that did not participate is NA.
translation.value: A list of strings the same length as string or pattern. A missing value is stringi._na.NA, which is JSON null.
translation.example:
from stringr.extract import str_extract
shopping_list = ["apples x4", "bag of flour", "bag of sugar", "milk x2"]
print(str_extract(shopping_list, "([a-z]+) of ([a-z]+)", group=1))
